model.vision: A dependable todo list a small team can adopt and rely on from day one.

objectives.statement: Let team members capture, reword, and discard tasks with no workarounds such as deleting and re-adding to fix a typo.
Give users full control over what counts as done, one task at a time or the whole list at once, always reversible.
Keep each list uncluttered by letting users sweep away all finished work in a single action.
Let users review their work the way they prefer (everything, what remains, or what is finished) while always knowing exactly how much remains.
Ensure no user ever loses their todos between visits, whether they close the app or restart their machine.
Let the team's automated agents work the same lists people do, with the same outcomes.
Be usable by a small team immediately, with no training beyond familiar todo-list conventions.

model.mission: Adopt the well-known TodoMVC behavior as the exact, non-negotiable contract instead of inventing features, keep every list safely held by the team's own infrastructure rather than the user's browser, and offer that one experience equally to people and to the team's agents wherever they already work.

items.definition: A person on the adopting team who keeps their own todo list and works it from one visit to the next.
One of the team's automated agents that works a todo list on a team member's behalf and must get exactly the outcomes a person would.
The small organization that adopts the todo list and holds every member's list on its own infrastructure rather than on any one member's device.
A single task on a list, made of a title and a completed state.
The ordered collection of todos belonging to one team member, with newly added todos placed at the end.
The free-text wording of a todo that says what the task is; a todo never has a blank title.
The state of a todo the user has marked done; reversible at any time.
The state of a todo that is not completed, meaning work still remains on it.
Put a new, active todo with the given title at the end of the user's list.
Change the title of an existing todo in place, keeping its identity and completed state, instead of discarding and re-adding it.
Take one todo off the list regardless of its completed state, leaving every other todo untouched.
Flip one todo between completed and active without affecting any other todo.
In one action, mark every todo completed, or, when every todo is already completed, mark every todo active again.
In one action, remove every completed todo from the list, leaving all active todos untouched; has no effect when nothing is completed.
Look at the list through one chosen view (All, Active, or Completed) without changing any todo.
One of three ways to review a list: All shows every todo, Active shows only active todos, Completed shows only completed todos; the current view is always visibly indicated.
The live count of active todos on the whole list, regardless of which view is being reviewed.
One stretch of time a team member or team agent spends working a list; the list must be exactly as left when the next visit begins.
Deciding whether submitted wording makes a usable title: wording that is empty or only whitespace is never accepted as a title.
Deciding that rewording a todo down to empty or whitespace-only wording discards that todo rather than leaving it with a blank title.
Dropping an in-progress reword so the todo keeps its original title unchanged.
Deciding what Toggle All does: if every todo is completed, all become active; otherwise, including a mixed list, all become completed.
Choosing which todos belong in the chosen view based only on their completed state.
Counting the active todos across the entire list after any change that could alter which todos are active.
Durably keep a newly added todo at the end of its owner's list.
Durably replace one todo's title with accepted new wording.
Durably take one todo off its owner's list.
Durably set one todo's state to completed or active.
Durably set every todo on a list to the same completed or active state in one step.
Durably remove every completed todo from a list in one step.
Retrieve a member's whole list, with every title and completed state, exactly as last kept.
The durable record, kept on the team's own infrastructure, of every member's todo list; it outlives closed sessions, device restarts, and restarts of the team's own services.

model.rationale: recommend DecompressedSolution: lowest in-band composite risk (0.332) at 140.0 days (App C risk-crossover exclusions applied)

items.name: Storage-technology volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the technology that durably holds the Team-Held List Record. WHY: the mission says lists live on 'the team's own infrastructure', and adopting teams don't share one storage stack today. One runs a managed relational database, another a single-node embedded store, another whatever its platform team already operates. LIKELIHOOD: high. Every adopting team is a different storage environment, and a team that moves platforms changes it again. EFFECT if unencapsulated: Record/Retitle/Remove/Set Completion/Purge/Recall logic would be bound to one vendor's API and query dialect. Each new team's infrastructure would ripple through every list operation and the durability guarantee that todos survive restarts.

items.name: Presentation-host volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: where a team member actually sees and works their list. WHY: the founder already needs two hosts at once, an ordinary browser web app and MCP Apps embedding inside the team's MCP-capable hosts. Team members differ in which they live in. LIKELIHOOD: high. More hosts are already arriving (other chat or IDE hosts with app embedding), and each renders, focuses, and handles events differently, which matters for in-place reword, Escape-to-abandon, and the always-visible current view. EFFECT if unencapsulated: the TodoMVC behaviors (view selection, items-left tally, blank-reword rule) would be re-implemented per host and drift apart. That breaks the mission's promise of one experience wherever people already work.

items.name: Agent-protocol volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the protocol through which the team's agents drive the lists (an MCP surface today, alongside a plain web API). WHY and LONGEVITY: the agent-tooling protocol space is young and churns fast. MCP alone has shipped several breaking or additive spec revisions per year since late 2024 (transports, auth, structured output, elicitation, apps). That rate falls well inside this system's multi-year lifespan, and the team's own agent tooling will move with it. LIKELIHOOD: near-certain within 12 months. EFFECT if unencapsulated: list operations would be coupled to one protocol revision's tool/transport shapes. Each spec change would ripple into the business behavior and risk agents getting different outcomes than people, which violates the 'same outcomes' objective.

items.name: List-access-policy volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the rule for which principals may read or change which todo list. WHY: today a list belongs to one team member, and the team's agents act on a member's behalf. How far an agent's delegation reaches (all of a member's list, read-only, only some actions such as Clear Completed) is exactly what teams tighten or loosen as they gain trust in their agents. LIKELIHOOD: medium-high over 1–3 years, as agent governance matures in every organization adopting agents. EFFECT if unencapsulated: ownership and delegation checks would be scattered across every add/reword/discard/toggle/purge path and both surfaces. A policy change would have to be found and changed everywhere, and one missed path leaks or corrupts another member's list. (Authentication itself is platform-owned. This entry covers only the business rule keyed on the principal the platform supplies.)

items.name: Change-propagation volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: how a change made to a list by one actor or surface reaches the other surfaces showing that same list. WHY: people and agents work the same lists concurrently through different hosts. The browser, MCP Apps hosts, and MCP clients each support a different freshness mechanism (push/stream, host-relayed notifications, or only re-fetch), and teams combine them differently. LIKELIHOOD: high. It varies across hosts today and changes as hosts add notification support. EFFECT if unencapsulated: the items-left count and the current view would show stale data whenever an agent changes a list a person has open. Each host's refresh mechanism would leak into the list behaviors themselves.

rejected.name: Toggle-all / clear-completed rule volatility
rejected.reason: The Aggregate Completion Decision and Clear Completed semantics are pinned by the TodoMVC contract, which the mission adopts as 'exact, non-negotiable', and every TodoMVC implementation does them identically. Changing them would change what the product is.

rejected.name: Title-acceptance volatility
rejected.reason: Rejecting empty or whitespace-only wording, and discarding on a blank reword, is a single trim-and-check conditional. A tweak (e.g. a max length) stays a conditional and never ripples across components.

rejected.name: View-set volatility
rejected.reason: All/Active/Completed is selection by one boolean. Even an added view would be another predicate over completed state, handled in the selection code, not by a new component.

rejected.name: Todo-attribute volatility (due dates, priorities, tags)
rejected.reason: The behavior contract explicitly lists due dates, priorities, and tags as out of scope and 'must not be assumed required'. Encapsulating them now would design for a different product.

rejected.name: List-ordering volatility (drag-to-reorder)
rejected.reason: New todos simply append to the end, and drag-to-reorder is explicitly excluded by the contract. Nothing in the brief points to custom ordering.

rejected.name: Undo/redo and completed-history volatility
rejected.reason: Undo/redo history is explicitly out of scope, and Clear Completed is a deliberate permanent sweep to keep the list uncluttered. Archiving finished work is a hypothetical future product.

rejected.name: Shared / multi-user list volatility
rejected.reason: Multi-user sharing is explicitly excluded, and each list belongs to one member. Who may act on a list is already covered by List-access-policy volatility, so a separate sharing seam would be speculative.

rejected.name: Offline-sync volatility
rejected.reason: Offline sync is explicitly out of scope, and the mission puts lists on team infrastructure rather than the device, so there is no business pressure for client-side replicas.

rejected.name: Authentication / sign-in volatility
rejected.reason: How team members and agents prove who they are is encapsulated by the platform's Security utility and front door (rc.Principal). A project seam would duplicate a utility, and this business is not identity.

rejected.name: Durability-guarantee volatility (survive restarts)
rejected.reason: Surviving tab closes, device restarts, and service restarts is the fixed guarantee of the Team-Held List Record. Whatever could change about it is the storage technology, so this is folded into Storage-technology volatility.

rejected.name: Hosting-environment volatility
rejected.reason: Where and how the service process runs (cloud, on-prem, scaling) is owned by the platform runtime doctrine and the per-project operational concepts, not by a business component. The only team-specific part, where list data lives, is Storage-technology volatility.

rejected.name: Web-API protocol volatility
rejected.reason: The plain web API and the MCP surface are both programmatic doors through which non-browser callers drive the same list operations. A change to either is the same underlying change, so this is folded into Agent-protocol volatility.

rejected.name: Concurrent-edit conflict volatility
rejected.reason: Each list has one owner plus the owner's own agents. Conflicting simultaneous rewords of the same todo are rare, and a simple last-write rule satisfies the contract. A conflict-resolution seam would be over-design. Keeping concurrent viewers fresh is Change-propagation volatility.

rejected.name: Agent-outcome-equivalence volatility
rejected.reason: 'Agents get the same outcomes as people' is a fixed property of the product, not a thing that changes. The only volatile part is the protocol agents speak, which is Agent-protocol volatility.

rejected.name: Behavior-contract volatility (TodoMVC itself)
rejected.reason: The mission adopts TodoMVC as the exact contract instead of inventing features. Changing the contract would mean a different product, not a change this one should absorb.

rejected.name: UI text / localization volatility
rejected.reason: 'Items left' wording and pluralization are display strings for a small team, handled by a formatter or resource table, not by architecture.

rejected.name: Logging / reporting block
rejected.reason: This is a siren-song reflex block. The brief has no reporting, analytics, or audit need, and Items Left is a live tally, not a report.

rejected.name: Team-scale / multi-tenancy volatility
rejected.reason: Each team holds its own lists on its own infrastructure for a small team. Cross-team tenancy and growth to large scale have no grounding in the brief, and scaling is platform-owned.

decisions.essenceRationale: Changing what is on a list and what counts as done is the one thing every adopting team buys, whatever host its people use and whichever agents act for them. Add, reword, discard, mark, toggle-all and clear-completed are all permutations of it: one principal asks for one change, the team's access policy admits or refuses it, the fixed TodoMVC rules decide the outcome, the team's own store keeps it, and every surface showing the list sees it. That shape is nearly immutable because the mission pins TodoMVC as the exact, non-negotiable contract. What sets it apart is that people and agents get identical outcomes through any surface, on team-held storage. It is an abstraction over the customer's six verbs, not any one of them.

decisions.essenceRationale: Coming back to find the list exactly as it was left, seen the way you want, with an honest count of what remains, is the 'dependable from day one' promise in the vision. Every customer relies on it on every visit, from every host, and agents rely on it before they act. Persistence across closed tabs, restarted laptops and restarted services, all three views, and the items-left counter are permutations of this one behavior: recall the team-held record, select a view of it, tally what is active, and keep the surface current. It almost never changes because the contract fixes the views and the tally. What sets it apart is that the record lives on the team's own infrastructure, not in a browser, and stays fresh while agents work the same list. That is an abstraction, not the 'filter' or 'counter' feature.

accessGrantingEngine.title: AccessGrantingEngine — decides whether a requester may read or make one change to a member's todo list. Pure, deterministic, side-effect free (no time, no RNG, no I/O, no global state), safe to call from Manager workflow code and to retry. Fail closed: any question it cannot positively match to a permitting rule is refused. A refusal is a normal decision (permitted=false with a reason), never an error; the error return is reserved and the implementation returns nil. The requester facts are the platform-supplied rc.Principal as ListManager reads it (subject, kind, delegation claims); they are never taken from a request payload, and the engine verifies no credential. Single operation by design: every one of the 12 dynamic views calls exactly DecideAccess and nothing else on this engine (App C §6.2a waived — the facet is one question; adding ops would be uncalled, TP-OP-REACHED).

AccessQuestion.description: One access question: may this requester perform this intent on this owner's list?

delegations.description: Delegations the requester holds (agents only; ignored for members).

owner.description: Subject id of the member whose list is targeted.

requesterSubject.description: rc.Principal.Subject of the request ListManager is serving.

Delegation.description: A grant a member has given an agent, as carried on the agent's platform principal claims and passed through by ListManager.

grantor.description: Subject id of the member who granted the delegation.

intents.description: The intents the agent may perform on the grantor's list. Empty means no reach.

Intent.description: What the requester wants to do to the list. Closed set; per-action granularity lets a delegation be narrowed to some actions (e.g. clearCompleted only). Anything else is refused.

RefusalReason.description: Why a question was refused; empty when permitted. Reasons never reveal whether another member's list exists.

RequesterKind.description: A team member acting for themselves, or a team agent acting on a member's behalf (ListManager maps rc.Principal.Kind user→member, application→agent).

listManager.title: ListManager — the list-keeping workflow (Change-propagation volatility): admit → (recall) → rule → keep → tally → publish, identical for every door (TodoWebApp, TodoMcpServer, TodoApi) and for members and agents alike. Thin orchestrator: access policy is AccessGrantingEngine's, TodoMVC rulings are ListRulingEngine's, storage is TodoListAccess's, transport is MessageBus's; ListManager branches only on outcomes they return (refused, blank, toggle target). Temporal-hosted; every op is one short workflow whose engine calls run in workflow code and whose TodoListAccess calls are Activities (retry only StoreUnavailable). The requester is rc.Principal, supplied by the platform; no op takes a credential or actor field. Every op names the TARGET list by `owner` (the subject id of the member whose list it is; empty = the requester's own list, rc.Principal.Subject). ListManager maps rc.Principal (kind user→member, application→agent; delegation claims→Delegation) into AccessQuestion and calls DecideAccess with the op's intent FIRST; on refusal nothing is recalled, ruled, kept, tallied or published. Change propagation (owned here, in one place): after every KEPT change — add, retitle, blank-reword removal, discard, mark, toggle all, clear completed — and only after the keep succeeded, ListManager calls MessageBus.Publish(ListChanged{owner}) carrying no list content; subscribers re-fetch through OpenList. Reads, refusals, a blank add and any failed keep publish nothing. Publish is total, so a kept change is never reported failed for propagation reasons. Tally after a change: ListManager takes the whole resulting list (the TodoList returned by SetAllCompletion/PurgeCompleted, otherwise a RecallList after the keep) and asks ListRulingEngine.TallyItemsLeft; it never counts itself. Concurrency is last-write-wins. Decisions on the SRS open questions: (1) owner is an explicit op param, admitted by AccessGrantingEngine; (2) a blank add is a no-op outcome (notAdded), not an error; (3) error model = ListError below; (4) every change returns ChangeOutcome {outcome, todo, itemsLeft}; (5) ListChanged is a bare per-owner signal; (6) ListManager mints the todo id deterministically from owner + the caller's requestId; (7) Publish cannot fail.

ChangeOutcome.description: Result of every change op. todo holds the affected todo for added, retitled and marked, and is empty (zero value) otherwise. itemsLeft is ListRulingEngine.TallyItemsLeft over the WHOLE resulting list, the same number OpenList would report next.

ListError.description: Error model for every operation. Refused (terminal): AccessGrantingEngine refused this requester this intent on this owner's list. It is decided before any read, so it never reveals whether the list or any todo exists; reason relays the engine's RefusalReason (notOwner, outsideDelegation, incompleteQuestion). TodoNotFound (terminal): RewordTodo or MarkTodo named a todo that the admitted owner's list does not hold, e.g. after a concurrent discard (mapped from TodoListAccess TodoNotFound). InvalidRequest (terminal): an empty todoId, a view outside all/active/completed (ListRulingEngine UnknownView), or TodoListAccess InvalidRequest. Unavailable (transient): TodoListAccess stayed StoreUnavailable after the Activity retry policy ran out. Nothing partial was kept and nothing was published, so the caller may retry the same op: every op is idempotent (see each op). Engine errors other than UnknownView are reported as Unavailable. No storage, engine or Temporal detail crosses this boundary.

reason.description: For Refused, the RefusalReason; otherwise empty.

ListView.description: The list as seen in one view. todos are the todos visible in the view, in list order (ListRulingEngine.SelectView). itemsLeft counts active todos across the whole list (TallyItemsLeft). totalCount is the length of the whole list, so a host can hide the list when it is empty and derive the completed count (totalCount - itemsLeft) for Clear completed and the toggle-all state, without another round trip.

owner.description: Subject id of the member whose list this is (the resolved owner).

Outcome.description: What a change op did. added: a new active todo was appended. notAdded: the wording was blank, so nothing was kept or published. retitled: the todo's title was replaced in place. removed: the todo is gone, either after DiscardTodo or after a reword to blank wording (TodoMVC); also returned when it was already absent, since discard is idempotent. marked: one todo's completed state was set. toggled: every todo was set to the ListRulingEngine-ruled target in one write. cleared: every completed todo was deleted in one write.

listRulingEngine.title: ListRulingEngine — the TodoMVC ruling shared by every host. Pure, deterministic, stateless: no I/O, no clock, no RNG, no global mutable state, so ListManager calls it directly from workflow code. It never sees principals and never logs todo content. Only caller: ListManager (sync). Publishes and subscribes to nothing. Idempotent by construction: the same inputs always give the same ruling. Decisions on the SRS open questions: (1) JudgeTitle returns the title trimmed of surrounding Unicode whitespace; (2) on an empty list JudgeToggleTarget rules markCompleted=false (vacuously every todo is completed, TodoMVC `every` semantics), which is a no-op for the caller; (3) a view outside all/active/completed is a contract error (UnknownView), never a crash; (4) the engine takes a minimal RuledTodo projection {id, title, completed}, not the TodoListAccess record; (5) no maximum title length; (6) blank is one ruling for add and reword, and ListManager acts on it (reject on add, discard on reword).

ItemsLeft.description: Count of active (not completed) todos across the whole list, whatever view is being reviewed.

RuledTodo.description: Minimal projection of a todo the ruling needs. id is opaque to the engine and only carried through so SelectView can return the visible todos in list order.

TitleRuling.description: accepted=false means the wording was empty or whitespace-only (blank). When accepted, title is the wording trimmed of surrounding whitespace, with inner content kept verbatim. When blank, title is empty.

ToggleTarget.description: The Toggle All target. markCompleted=false means mark every todo active, which happens when every todo is already completed, including the empty list. markCompleted=true means mark every todo completed, which covers both mixed and all-active lists.

View.description: The chosen TodoMVC view. Selection depends only on completed state.

VisibleTodos.description: The todos visible in the chosen view, in their original list order.

messageBus.title: MessageBus — in-process, best-effort pub/sub carrier for bare per-owner ListChanged signals. Publish (ListManager, last step of every kept change) is total and non-blocking. Subscribe (TodoWebApp, TodoMcpServer) is a sequence-cursored long-poll whose lifecycle is the caller's context.

ListChanged.description: Publish input: the named member's list changed. Carries NO list content (no todos, titles or counts), so the bus can never leak list data across members; subscribers re-fetch through ListManager.OpenList, which passes AccessGrantingEngine. Publish is total and never returns an error: it increments the owner's per-owner sequence and wakes every Subscribe waiting on that owner without waiting on any subscriber, so a slow, dead or absent subscriber can never delay or fail a kept change. A publish with an empty owner is a silent no-op. No idempotency key is needed: a duplicate publish only advances the counter and costs at most one extra re-fetch. Safe for concurrent use; owners are isolated from each other.

owner.description: Principal id of the member whose list changed.

ListChangedNotice.description: Subscribe result: the owner's list changed at least once after the subscriber's afterSequence. Subscribe returns at once if the owner's current sequence > afterSequence; otherwise it blocks until the next Publish for that owner. Rapid publishes MAY coalesce into one notice carrying the latest sequence. Errors: the context error when the caller cancels (the tab or MCP session closed; all waiter state is released, and there is no Unsubscribe op), and an invalid-argument error for an empty owner or a negative afterSequence. Client loop: Subscribe, then re-fetch with OpenList, then Subscribe(afterSequence = notice.sequence). Semantics: in-process, single instance, at-most-once, best-effort; the monotone sequence preserves per-owner order and closes the gap between calls.

owner.description: Principal id of the member whose list changed (equals the subscribed owner).

sequence.description: The owner's change counter after the latest publish: starts at 1 and increases monotonically per owner within one bus instance.

schema.description: Principal id whose list to watch. Clients MUST pass only the principal they already served through ListManager.OpenList; owner scoping is the Client's duty.

AccessError.description: Error model for every operation. kind TodoNotFound: terminal; the owner's list holds no todo with that id (RetitleTodo, SetCompletion) — an id belonging to another owner is reported exactly as unknown. kind InvalidRequest: terminal; empty owner/todoId/title, or a todoId already recorded for a different owner. kind StoreUnavailable: transient; the store could not be reached or the write not confirmed, nothing partial was applied; retry with backoff. todo-web-app.content:
# UI Design Concept — TodoWebApp (browser surface)

Design concept only. This document contains no production code. It covers every requirement in the committed UX Requirements for `todo-web-app` (R-ADD … R-READ-REFUSED, N-*) for the single persona that surface serves, **Team Member**. Each screen, region, flow and state below carries the requirement id it traces to. Nothing here adds scope beyond those ids.

## 0. Design principles (from the N-* constraints)
- **P1 Familiar TodoMVC layout and gestures** (N-FAMILIAR, N-CONTRACT). The page uses the standard TodoMVC structure and interactions: a header input, a list with checkboxes, double-click to edit, a destroy button, and a footer with the count, filters and Clear completed. Members need no instructions.
- **P2 Show rulings, never compute them** (N-PARITY, N-CONTRACT; System: the Client holds no business rules). The surface never trims or judges a title. It never decides the toggle target, filters todos into a view, or counts items left. Every value it shows comes from `ListManager` (`ChangeOutcome`, `ListView`). For presentation only, the surface derives `completedCount = totalCount − itemsLeft` (as the contract documents) to decide whether Clear completed is shown and how toggle-all looks. It never uses that value to decide an outcome.
- **P3 No optimistic mutation** (N-PARITY, N-DURABLE). The list on screen changes only after `ListManager` reports the change was kept. Then the surface re-fetches `openList(currentView)`. As a result, the screen always shows the kept record, never a guess.
- **P4 Live by default** (N-FRESH, R-SYNC). While the list is open, the surface stays subscribed to `ListChanged` for this owner. On each notice it re-fetches through `openList`.
- **P5 No browser-held list data** (N-DURABLE, R-INTACT). The surface keeps no todos in local or session storage. Only the URL holds the chosen view.

## 1. Screen inventory
The surface has **one screen**, **List screen**. It is a single page with three regions and one overlay-free status strip. There are no other screens, and the surface has no settings, account or help pages, because no requirement asks for them.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    todos                     │  page title
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [status strip — hidden unless a notice]      │  §4 states
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [❯] What needs to be done?                   │  HEADER: toggle-all + new-todo input
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ( ) Buy milk                             [×] │  MAIN: todo rows
│ (✓) ~~Call plumber~~                     [×] │
│ ( ) Book flights                         [×] │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 2 items left   All | Active | Completed   Clear completed │  FOOTER
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1.1 Header region
| Element | Component | Behaviour | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page title “todos” | heading (h1) | Static. | N-FAMILIAR |
| New-todo input | single-line text field, placeholder “What needs to be done?”, autofocus on load | **Enter** submits the raw wording as typed through `addTodo`. The field clears only on outcome `added` or `notAdded`. On an error the field keeps its text so the member can retry. | R-ADD |
| Toggle-all control | checkbox (chevron style) labelled “Mark all as complete” for assistive tech | Shown only when `totalCount > 0`. Shown checked when `itemsLeft == 0`. Activating it calls `toggleAll()`. The engine picks the target, not the surface. | R-TOGGLE-ALL |

### 1.2 Main region (todo list)
Hidden entirely when `totalCount == 0` (N-FAMILIAR). Renders `ListView.todos` in the order received.

**Todo row (view mode)**
| Element | Component | Behaviour | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Completion checkbox | round checkbox, labelled by the title | Toggling calls `markTodo(todoId, !completed)`. Doing it again reverses the change. | R-MARK |
| Title | label. Completed rows show strikethrough and muted text. | **Double-click** enters edit mode. | R-REWORD, R-MARK |
| Destroy button | “×” icon button, visible on row hover or focus, accessible name “Delete <title>” | Calls `discardTodo(todoId)`. | R-DISCARD |

**Todo row (edit mode)**, one row at most at a time
| Element | Behaviour | Trace |
|---|---|---|
| Edit field pre-filled with the kept title, focused, caret at end | **Enter** or **blur** commits the edit with `rewordTodo(todoId, wording)`. **Escape** abandons it: the row goes back to view mode with the original title and no call is made. | R-REWORD |
| Outcome `retitled` | The row shows the returned title in place, with the same position and completed state. | R-REWORD |
| Outcome `removed` (blank wording) | The row disappears (blank reword rule). The surface sends blank wording as typed and lets the engine rule on it. | R-REWORD |

### 1.3 Footer region
Hidden when `totalCount == 0`.
| Element | Component | Behaviour | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Items-left count | text: “**N** item left” / “**N** items left” (singular only when N = 1) | Always shows `itemsLeft` from the latest `ListView`/`ChangeOutcome`, so it counts the whole list in every view. | R-LEFT, R-TALLY-AFTER |
| View filters | three links: All, Active, Completed. They are bound to the URL (`#/`, `#/active`, `#/completed`). The selected link is outlined and carries `aria-current`. | Choosing one updates the URL and calls `openList(view)`. No todo is changed. | R-VIEW |
| Clear completed | text button | Shown only when `completedCount > 0`. Calls `clearCompleted()`. | R-CLEAR |

## 2. Flows (per use case / variation)
Every change flow follows the same skeleton (UC1, `work-the-list`): **gesture → one `ListManager` change op → on success, apply the `ChangeOutcome.itemsLeft` immediately and re-fetch `openList(currentView)` → render**. On error, see §4. The surface sends one request per gesture, and each request carries a fresh request id so the server can deduplicate retries. A row whose request is in flight is marked busy and does not accept a second gesture until the outcome arrives.

| Flow | Steps | Outcomes shown | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-ADD | type wording → Enter → `addTodo(wording)` | `added`: the field clears and the new active todo appears at the end of the list (if the current view shows it). `notAdded`: the field clears and the list is unchanged. There is no error message, because a blank add is a silent no-op in TodoMVC. | R-ADD |
| F-REWORD | double-click title → edit → Enter/blur → `rewordTodo` / Escape → abandon | `retitled` in place. `removed` deletes the row. Escape keeps the original title and makes no call. | R-REWORD |
| F-DISCARD | hover/focus row → × → `discardTodo` | `removed`: only that row goes and the other rows are untouched. | R-DISCARD |
| F-MARK | click checkbox → `markTodo(id, completed)` | `marked`: the row's style flips and the count updates. In the Active or Completed view the row leaves that view after the re-fetch. | R-MARK |
| F-TOGGLE-ALL | click toggle-all → `toggleAll()` | `toggled`: every row flips to the ruled target and the toggle-all state follows `itemsLeft`. | R-TOGGLE-ALL |
| F-CLEAR | click Clear completed → `clearCompleted()` | `cleared`: completed rows go and active rows stay. The button hides when `completedCount` becomes 0. | R-CLEAR |
| F-OPEN | page load or return → read view from URL (default `all`) → `openList(view)` → render → start subscription | Shows the full kept list exactly as last stored, with titles and completed states. | R-INTACT, R-LEFT |
| F-VIEW | click filter or navigate the URL hash → `openList(view)` | Only that view's todos appear, the filter is highlighted, and the count is unchanged. | R-VIEW, R-LEFT |
| F-SYNC | subscription notice → `openList(currentView)` → re-subscribe after the notice's sequence | Changes from another browser, MCP Apps host or Team Agent appear without a reload. A row in edit mode keeps the member's draft. If that todo disappeared, edit mode closes and a notice says it was removed elsewhere. | R-SYNC, N-FRESH |

## 3. Live-update behaviour (R-SYNC)
- The subscription starts after the first successful `openList` and lasts as long as the tab is open. Closing the tab ends it.
- Each `ListChanged` notice triggers one re-fetch of the current view. A burst of notices may arrive as a single notice, and the surface re-fetches only once for it.
- The surface ignores a notice that arrives while its own change is in flight, because it already re-fetches after its own outcome. Notices that arrive afterwards are applied as usual.
- If the subscription drops (network), the surface reconnects with backoff. After reconnecting it re-fetches once, so no change is missed.

## 4. States
| State | Trigger | Presentation | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| S-LOADING | the first `openList` is pending | Header input visible but disabled. A quiet “Loading your list…” line in the main region. | R-INTACT |
| S-EMPTY | `totalCount == 0` | Only the header input is shown. Toggle-all, the main region and the footer are hidden (TodoMVC convention). | R-ADD, N-FAMILIAR |
| S-LIST | `totalCount > 0` | Header, main and footer as in §1. | R-INTACT, R-VIEW, R-LEFT |
| S-VIEW-EMPTY | `totalCount > 0` but the view has no todos (e.g. Completed with none completed) | Empty main region. The footer still shows the count and filters. | R-VIEW |
| S-ROW-EDITING | double-click on a title | Edit field replaces the label. Other rows stay interactive. | R-REWORD |
| S-ROW-BUSY | a change for that row is in flight | Controls disabled, with subtle reduced opacity. | R-MARK, R-DISCARD, R-REWORD |
| S-READ-REFUSED | `openList` → `ListError.kind = Refused` | The whole list area is replaced by: “This list is outside your reach.” No todos, counts or hints about whether the list exists. Header input and footer hidden. No subscription. | R-READ-REFUSED |
| S-CHANGE-REFUSED | change op → `Refused` | Status strip (polite live region): “That change is outside your reach — nothing was changed.” The list stays exactly as it was, and an add or reword input keeps its text. The strip dismisses on the next action or after a few seconds. | R-REFUSED |
| S-TODO-GONE | `rewordTodo` / `markTodo` → `TodoNotFound` | Status strip: “That todo was removed elsewhere.” The surface re-fetches the current view. | R-SYNC, N-FRESH |
| S-UNAVAILABLE | any op → `Unavailable`, or a network failure | Status strip: “Couldn’t reach your list — nothing was changed.” with a **Retry** button that repeats the same op with the same request id. On first load the main region shows the same message with Retry instead. | N-DURABLE, R-INTACT |
| S-INVALID | `InvalidRequest` (for example a bad view in the URL hash) | An unknown hash falls back to `#/` (All). Other invalid requests show the generic unavailable strip. The surface does not invent its own validation. | R-VIEW |
| S-LIVE-RECONNECTING | the subscription dropped | Small unobtrusive “Reconnecting…” text in the footer. The list stays usable. | R-SYNC |

## 5. Component selection (presentation-level, framework-neutral)
- **NewTodoInput** (text field), **ToggleAllCheckbox**, **TodoList** → **TodoItem** (view/edit modes: checkbox, label, destroy button, edit field), **Footer** → **ItemsLeftCount**, **ViewFilters**, **ClearCompletedButton**, **StatusStrip** (an aria-live polite region).
- **ListClient adapter** (not visual). It is the one place that calls `ListManager`'s `addTodo | rewordTodo | discardTodo | markTodo | toggleAll | clearCompleted | openList` and keeps the `subscribe(ListChanged)` loop. Components never call the backend directly. This matches the System relationships `todo-web-app → list-manager` and `todo-web-app → message-bus`, and nothing beyond them.
- **View state**: the current view lives in the URL hash only. All list data comes from the latest `ListView`.
- Styling follows the familiar TodoMVC visual language (centred card, light theme, strikethrough for completed) so members recognise it immediately (N-FAMILIAR). The surface uses its own stylesheet and does not reproduce anyone else's assets.

## 6. Accessibility and input
- Every control can be reached and operated by keyboard. On a focused row, Enter or F2 starts editing (the keyboard equivalent of double-click), Enter commits and Escape abandons.
- Checkboxes and the destroy button have accessible names that include the todo title. The selected filter has `aria-current="page"`. Status-strip messages go out through a polite live region.
- After discard or clear, focus moves to the next row, or to the new-todo input when no rows remain.
- Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast. Completed rows never rely on colour alone, because strikethrough also marks them.

## 8. Open points for review
1. **Commit on blur.** TodoMVC commits an edit on blur. The UX Requirements say only “commit or abandon”, so this concept follows TodoMVC (N-CONTRACT). Reviewers should confirm.
2. **Change-refused copy.** The UX Requirements require that the member be told the change is outside their reach. The exact wording above is a proposal for ux-reviewer.
3. **Draft kept on concurrent change.** A row in edit mode keeps the member's draft when a remote change re-fetches the list (F-SYNC). This avoids losing typed text. It does not change any rule.
